item.title: French students clash with police as school protests spread nationwide
item.description: Footage shows pupils in Paris, Toulouse and Lille clashing with police as they demand better school resources, warning protests will continue nationwide.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 2nd, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 2nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: The solar system will fall apart far sooner than anyone thought, scientists say
item.description: Earth will be long gone by then, but new research shows the outer planets will be thrown out too, and a billion times earlier than expected, according to astrophysics research.

item.title: G7 agrees 100 million-barrel emergency oil release amid US pressure over diesel
item.description: The G7, led by France, announced the release of 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil after Trump threatened a ban of diesel exports.

item.title: Putin says all weapons 'on agenda' if Russia's Kaliningrad attacked
item.description: Russia would consider using "all types of weapons" if its exclave of Kaliningrad was attacked, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Thursday, while insisting that Moscow had "no intention of attacking anyone."

item.title: Assisi marks 800 years since St Francis's death and remains a symbol of peace and dialogue
item.description: Today we honour Saint Francis, symbol of peace and diplomacy. On the 800th anniversary of his death, Euronews revisits his meeting with the sultan of Egypt and what this charismatic figure still has to teach us.

item.title: Beyond K-pop and cinema: Major Korean exhibition brings centuries of art and belief to London
item.description: The exhibition includes 10 national treasures and official Korean designations recognising their cultural importance, with most exhibits drawn from the collection of late Samsung billionaire Lee Kun-Hee.

item.title: 5,000 drones turn China’s night sky into a giant light show
item.description: A fleet of 5,000 drones forms fighter jets, robots, planes and horses over Nanchang as China marks National Day with a spectacular night show.

item.title: Spanish Congress rejects housing laws despite Sánchez's warning: 'They'll be judged sooner than they think'
item.description: Spanish Congress rejects two key housing measures aimed at quelling public uproar over housing affordability. The bills' rejection after last-minute talks leaves Pedro Sánchez's government without two key housing measures and exposes its struggle to win support in Congress.

item.title: Iconic London hotel Dukes is set to reopen in mid-2027
item.description: The property, which is home to the legendary martini spot Dukes Bar, will be operated by Minor Hotels.

item.title: Mobile ebola laboratory cuts diagnosis times for patients in Congo
item.description: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern DRC, is cutting Ebola testing times, with results available within 24 hours and sometimes as quickly as six.

item.title: France and Germany lead push to keep military space powers in national hands
item.description: Germany and France are among seven countries calling for the proposed European Space Shield to be rebuilt around protecting EU space systems – with military space capabilities kept national.

item.title: EU farmers face falling produce prices as fuel and fertiliser costs rise
item.description: Eurostat figures show a widening gap between the prices farmers receive and those they pay, as EU ministers discuss support and farming groups demand help.

item.title: Inside Soitec, the French tech company powering the global semiconductor industry
item.description: From smartphones to data centres, the French company’s advanced silicon substrates underpin technologies used around the world. Valérie Gauriat went inside its production site in the French Alps.

item.title: French government forecasts 1% growth in 2027: What do experts think?
item.description: France's High Council for Public Finance calls the government's 1.0% growth forecast for the 2027 budget "optimistic", as economists warn of a possible "slippage" and the executive still has to secure approval.

item.title: From ocean waste to fabric: inside Spain’s sustainable fashion revolution
item.description: Every year, more than 12 million tonnes of plastic ends up in our oceans. Spanish fashion company Ecoalf transforms marine waste and discarded materials into fabrics and clothing through a circular supply chain. But can sustainable fashion transform an industry built on overproduction?

item.title: Can releasing more of Europe’s emergency reserves bring diesel prices down?
item.description: The EU says it is ready for collective action with the IEA on a fresh emergency release. Analysts say releasing diesel reserves could lower pump prices within days, but would offer only short-term relief.

item.title: Casa de México in Madrid unveils 2026 Day of the Dead altar inspired by Michoacán and Agustín Lara
item.description: Casa de México in Madrid unveils "Viva la vida!", its 2026 Day of the Dead altar honouring Agustín Lara, inspired by Michoacán and the monarch butterfly, with a musical tour. Free entry from 2 October to 8 November.

item.title: Finland's government survives confidence vote after Israel visit row
item.description: Finland's government on Friday survived a parliamentary vote of confidence called over the government's Middle East policy following a criticised visit to Israel by the defence minister.

item.title: AI decodes 217-year-old Napoleonic letter in 6 hours
item.description: An engineer used artificial intelligence to decode a military cypher from the Napoleonic era that had gone unsolved for more than two centuries.

item.title: Andy Burnham is rethinking the UK’s ties with the EU. What are his options?
item.description: Burnham’s decision to put the prospect of EU membership back on the table has caught attention in Brussels. But any attempt to unpick Brexit could come with conditions and difficult trade-offs.

item.title: Switzerland's President Guy Parmelin says he will quit government at end of year
item.description: A winegrower by trade, Parmelin is from the French-speaking western canton of Vaud. He is from the hard-right Swiss People's Party (SVP), which is the biggest in the country.

item.title: France weighs emergency oil release as US pressure mounts ahead of G7 call
item.description: France is set to present a plan to release emergency oil stocks following US pressure, with Paris considering a combined release of crude oil and diesel. President Emmanuel Macron will hold a G7 call on Friday.

item.title: UK scraps charges to seat children with parents on flights, and for simple name errors
item.description: The new rules, announced by UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, have now come into force.

item.title: Man City lodges 'comprehensive' appeal after being found guilty of financial rule-breaking
item.description: According to the Premier League, potential sanctions against City could be a reprimand, a fine, a suspension, points deduction or, in the worst case, expulsion from the competition.

item.title: US sends third carrier strike group to Middle East in biggest buildup since 2003
item.description: The USS Theodore Roosevelt left San Diego on Sunday accompanied by a Marine expeditionary unit of more than 2,000 troops, bringing the potential total US military presence in the region to more than 60,000.

item.title: T-shirts instead of winter coats: What a warm October reveals about winter
item.description: At the start of October, temperatures of up to 25C give parts of Europe a last taste of late summer. Yet, according to an old farmers' rule, a warm autumn can herald a severe winter. What do the statistics and meteorologists say?

item.title: Video shows bear slamming into car in northern Japan
item.description: A brown bear slammed its body against a car in northern Japan after two bears were spotted on a road in Hokkaido. The larger bear, believed to be the mother, approached the vehicle before running away with its cub. The driver was unharmed, and police have released dashcam footage of the encounter.

item.title: Hungary and Ukraine edge towards deal that could unlock EU talks
item.description: Kyiv will propose a new law on minority education rights, with a vote expected in October. Budapest has blocked EU accession talks until Ukraine adopts the laws agreed under an 11-point plan on Hungarians in Transcarpathia.

item.title: Italy's firefighting planes return home after summer battling blazes across Europe
item.description: Western Europe recorded its hottest summer on record, with some 540,000 hectares going up in smoke across the European Union between mid-June and early September.

item.title: DiscoverEU applications now open: Thousands of free travel passes for young Europeans up for grabs
item.description: Applications for the scheme are open until 15 October, giving eligible young Europeans the chance to explore the continent by train and other sustainable transport, with discounts on accommodation, culture and more.

item.title: Fact check: What's going on with Spain's 'Maricarmen' housing protests?
item.description: Spanish protests against the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen have led to misleading claims about Spain's housing activists and the wider rental crisis.

item.title: Schools closed, services slowed and flights cancelled: strikes hit Portugal
item.description: Three CGTP unions have called a strike for Friday, disrupting schools, public services, councils and rubbish collection. An easyJet cabin crew walkout is also causing flight delays nationwide.

item.title: Could the future of AI data centres be in space? Google wants to find out
item.description: The tech giant has launched a prototype satellite carrying its AI chips to explore whether solar powered infrastructure in orbit could one day support large-scale computing.

item.title: European diesel reserves cover 10 days of the world's demands, expert says
item.description: "Even if all of 300 million barrels of European reserves are released, it will only cover around 10 to 11 days of the world's diesel demand", energy expert, Osama Rizvi tells Euronews and Europe Today, about President Trump's call to European countries to release some of their diesel reserves.

item.title: EU adds €130 million to drone funding in border security push
item.description: The Commission is adding €130 million for drone technology as Brussels steps up border surveillance and prepares to strengthen Frontex’s role.

item.title: Hundreds of high schools in France close as new protests against conditions erupt
item.description: The students say their school hours are excessively long, conditions inadequate including overheated classrooms, and that there are too many staff absences.

item.title: Cornell University gang rape allegations: case sparks debate among US students
item.description: New York prosecutors have reopened an investigation into an alleged sexual assault involving seven members of Cornell University's Chi Phi fraternity in 2024.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 2nd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 2nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: New York hosts secret dîner en blanc with Parisian belle époque theme
item.description: Thousands dressed in white gather at a secret New York location for Dîner en Blanc, an annual outdoor dinner with a Parisian Belle Époque theme.

item.title: Meloni asks Brussels for fiscal leeway as energy shock squeezes Italy
item.description: Italian prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is urging the European Commission again to relax the EU's fiscal rules, saying that higher inflation due to soaring energy prices is squeezing households and businesses, according to a letter seen by Euronews.

item.title: Bonds steady as French borrowing costs hit 24-year high and UK 30-year yields top 6%
item.description: Government bond markets steadied on Friday morning after a sell-off pushed France's 10-year borrowing costs to their highest since 2002, lifted UK 30-year yields above 6% for the first time since 1998 and drove the benchmark US 10-year yield to a 24-year high.

item.title: Eurozone inflation spikes to 3.8%: Is your country on the worst list?
item.description: Eurozone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, a three-year high above forecasts. Energy drove the spike. See where prices rose fastest.

item.title: New severe weather alert issued for Crete as heavy rainfall already recorded
item.description: Disruption caused by the recent bout of severe weather continues, with authorities warning that further problems may arise as conditions remain unsettled.

item.title: These are the easiest countries to be a digital nomad in, according to a new study
item.description: Holafly’s Digital Nomad Friction Index 2026 looked at factors such as visa complexity, banking access, healthcare and cost of living.

item.title: What does music look like? This British artist paints what he hears
item.description: Sounds can sometimes interrupt Andrew’s thoughts, but he sees synaesthesia as an inseparable part of his life.

item.title: Did Trump order Maduro’s kidnapping based on Grok’s advice?
item.description: The US president spent hours in the White House asking Musk’s AI chatbot questions, including how Venezuelans would react if the US captured Maduro, Time magazine reports.

item.title: Traffic gridlocked in Ukraine's capital as Russian drone strikes close key bridge
item.description: Ukraine has long feared an attack on its major transportation bridges since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

item.title: EU holds crisis meeting as US pressure mounts to release emergency oil stocks
item.description: EU countries and the European Commission are holding talks on Friday that could pave the way for a new emergency oil reserves release, as pressure from Washington mounts. Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen told Euronews a fresh emergency release is "a possibility".

item.title: Trans-Caspian Corridor: Europe and Central Asia target faster trade
item.description: Transit along the Trans-Caspian Corridor currently takes around 35 days, with a target of cutting this to between 15 and 20. Officials say customs, digital systems and predictable border procedures are as important as new railways and ports.
